1.
The present claim petition arises out of road accident in which one Gitesh Kumar, aged about 55 years, suffered fatal injury resulting in his death.

An application u/s 166(1) Motor Vehicle Act was accordingly filed by the claimant (1) Sangita Devi (wife of deceased), (2) Vidya Devi (mother of deceased),
(3) Ashish Kumar (son of deceased), (4) Roji Kumari and (5)
Khushi Kumari (daughters of deceased) as dependents of the deceased.
2. Brief facts of the case are that on 06.10.2021 at about 01:00 PM, Sh. Gitesh Kumar (since deceased) along with his son Ashish Kumar was going to Sampaul Bazar on Scooty bearing no. BR-50H-7091.

When they reached NH-57, Simrahi Bazar,
West Gandhi Nagar, a Scorpio car bearing no.BR-07-PC-4342 (hereinafter referred to the offending vehicle) came at very high speed driven in a rash and negligent manner and hit the scooty of the victim.
As a result, both were dragged to a few meters on the road and victim Gitesh Kumar died on the spot.
Victim was removed to Raghopur Hospital where his postmortem was conducted.

18. As regards entitlement of the petitioner to compensation,
petitioner no. 1 is claimed to be widow/wife of the deceased,

Since, petitioner no.3 and 4 both are major and no dependency has been shown on the deceased, petitioner no.3 and 4 are not entitle to compensation under the head of dependency.
Petitioner no.1, 2 and 5 are entitle to compensation under the head of dependency.

The relevant principles for ascertainment of compensation are quoted here under:
 BASIC PRINCIPLES  "9.

The issues to  be determined by the Tribunal to arrive at the loss of  dependency are (i) additions/deductions to be made for  arriving at the income; (ii) the deduction to be made  towards the personal living expenses of the deceased;
 and (iii) the multiplier to be applied with reference of  the age of the deceased.
If these determinants are  standardized, there will be uniformity and consistency  in the decisions.
There will lesser need for detailed  evidence.
It will also be easier for the insurance  companies to settle accident claims without delay.

To  have uniformity and consistency, Tribunals should  determine compensation in cases of death, by the  following well settled steps : -
 Step 1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be  determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should  be made in regard to the amount which the deceased  would have spent on himself by way of personal and  living expenses.
The balance, which is considered to be  the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the  multiplicand.

Step 2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
 Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of  active career, the appropriate multiplier should be  selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number  of years he would have lived or worked but for the  accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in  life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with  reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table  with reference to the age of the deceased.
Step 3 (Actual calculation)

It is  because a coordinate Bench of the same strength cannot  take a contrary view than what has been held by another  coordinate Bench.
 (ii) As Rajesh has not taken note of the decision in  Reshma Kumari, which was delivered at earlier point of  time, the decision in Rajesh is not a binding precedent.

should be made.
The  addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was  between 40 to 50 years.

 methodology and considerations for assessing/ascertaining just compensation in road vehicular death cases laid down in Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6 SCC.
Basically only three facts need to be established by  the claimants for assessing compensation in the case of  death :-
 (a) age of the deceased; (b) income of the deceased;
 and the (c) the number of dependents.
The balance, which is considered to be  the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the  multiplicand.
This does not mean ascertaining the number  of years he would have lived or worked but for the  accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in  life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with  reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
In regard to bachelors, normally,
 50% is deducted as personal and living expenses,
 because it is assumed that a bachelor would tend to  spend more on himself.

In the absence of evidence to the contrary,

The  addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was  between 40 to 50 years.

An addition of 25% where the deceased  was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where  the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should  be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
